```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.pos = "htbp")
template_dir <- "../../_shared/template"
source(file.path(template_dir, "viscount_rmd_helpers.R"))
library(jsonlite)

mod_data <- fromJSON("southeast.json5", simplifyVector = FALSE)
sett_data <- fromJSON("southeast_settlements.json", simplifyVector = FALSE)
ledger_data <- fromJSON("southeast_source_ledger.json5", simplifyVector = FALSE)

clean_text <- function (txt) {
  s <- as.character(txt)
  s <- gsub("Existing Verified ", "", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("coordinate/alias", "coordinate or alias", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub(" / ", " and ", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub(" & ", " and ", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("&", " and ", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("_", " ", s, fixed = TRUE)
  return(s)
}

short_region <- function (rid) {
  if (identical(rid, "se_carolina_piedmont_santee")) return("Carolina Piedmont")
  if (identical(rid, "se_georgia_savannah_ocmulgee_etowah")) return("Georgia Basins")
  if (identical(rid, "se_alabama_tombigbee_moundville")) return("Alabama-Tombigbee")
  if (identical(rid, "se_peninsular_florida_apalachicola")) return("Florida-Apalachicola")
  return(clean_text(rid))
}

fmt_yr_label <- function (y) {
  if (y < 0) paste0(abs(y), "BC") else paste0(y, "AD")
}

fmt_span_pop <- function (pop_list) {
  yrs <- as.integer(names(pop_list))
  ord <- order(yrs)
  yrs <- yrs[ord]
  vals <- vapply(yrs, function (y) as.numeric(pop_list[[as.character(y)]]), numeric(1))
  pk_idx <- which.max(vals)
  paste0(viscount_fmt_pop(vals[pk_idx]), " (", fmt_yr_label(yrs[pk_idx]), ")")
}

fmt_period_span <- function (pop_list) {
  yrs <- sort(as.integer(names(pop_list)))
  if (min(yrs) == max(yrs)) fmt_yr_label(min(yrs)) else paste0(fmt_yr_label(min(yrs)), "-", fmt_yr_label(max(yrs)))
}
```

# Abstract

This gazetteer documents 115 archaeological and early contact settlements across the Southeast Hydrological Unit (HU 03) from 10000BC to 1600AD. Out of 220 candidate entries evaluated in the regional source ledger, 115 sites meet spatial and demographic inclusion thresholds, whereas 105 duplicate coordinate and alias records within 2 km are consolidated into canonical entries during deduplication. The inventory traces eleven millennia of aggregation from Palaeoindian spring and river-terrace sites at Cactus Hill (45 in 10000BC), Page-Ladson (25 in 10000BC) and Topper (25 in 10000BC), through Archaic wetland and shell-ring communities including Windover (120 at 5200BC), Stallings Island (260 at 2000BC) and Sapelo Shell Ring (310 at 1500BC), Middle Woodland Kolomoki (1,65k at 600AD) and major Mississippian capitals led by Etowah (4,2k at 1300AD), Moundville (3,5k at 1300AD), Mound Key (2,4k at 1550AD), Coosa (2,2k at 1550AD), Mabila (2,2k at 1540AD), Okmulgi (2,1k at 1100AD), Mulberry (1,8k at 1500AD), Lake Jackson Mounds (1,6k at 1500AD), Cofitachequi (1,45k at 1500AD) and Bottle Creek (1,4k at 1400AD), down to early European footholds at Fort Caroline (300 in 1564AD) and Roanoke Island (117 in 1587AD).

# Background

Archaeological fieldwork across the Atlantic Piedmont and Gulf Coastal Plain confirms repeated cycles of civic mound construction, estuarine village persistence and regional dispersal [@knight1998; @king2003; @kelly2025]. While Kelly et al. [@kelly2025] radiocarbon summed probability curves (N = 1.716) peak around 1169AD, platform-mound capitals such as Etowah and Moundville reached their largest residential footprints near 1250AD to 1325AD before giving way to sixteenth-century regional provinces, notably Cofitachequi, Coosa, Mabila, Apalachee and Calusa, recorded during early Spanish and English expeditions [@hudson1997; @milanich1995; @quinn1985].

# Methodology

## Inclusion Criteria and Schema Audit

All 220 candidates in the regional source ledger were checked for exact WGS84 coordinates, multi-phase residential footprints or garrison enumerations and distinct non-overlapping boundaries. Each of the 115 included entries is linked directly to its encompassing hydrological sub-region and primary archaeological or historical literature cited here and in the ledger.

## Settlement Size Calibration

Pre-contact town counts combine palisaded village hectares, excavated structure floors and mound-precinct residential zones across Etowah, Moundville, Town Creek, Bottle Creek and Mound Key [@knight1998; @king2003; @coe1995; @brown2003; @thompson2016]. Archaic and Woodland shell-mound and wetland loci, notably Windover, Stallings Island, Kolomoki and Irene Mound, derive from excavated midden extents and mortuary-catchment models [@doran2002; @sassaman2006; @caldwell1941]. Sixteenth-century colonial posts at Fort Caroline and Roanoke Island reflect documented French Huguenot and English expeditionary rosters [@milanich1995; @quinn1985].

# Testing and Validation

Ledger reconciliation and spatial containment checks across all 220 candidates cleared zero-error tolerance at GMT+0:

1. **Included Settlements**: 115 sites (25 in Carolina Piedmont-Santee, 29 in Georgia Basins, 28 in Alabama-Tombigbee and 33 in Florida-Apalachicola).
2. **Excluded Candidates**: 105 duplicate coordinate and alias records within 2 km consolidated into canonical settlement entries.

# Results

## Top 45 Pre-Contact and Contact Settlements

Table \ref{tab:se-included} ranks the leading 45 settlements by peak population descending out of the 115 catalogued sites in HU 03. Earliest occupation begins at 10000BC along the Nottoway, Savannah and Aucilla corridors at Cactus Hill (45-120), Topper (25-55) and Page-Ladson (25-35), followed by Early Archaic Windover (80-120 across 6200BC-5200BC) [@doran2002] and Late Archaic Savannah and Atlantic shell-ring sites led by Stallings Island (260 at 2000BC), Fig Island (280 at 1900BC), St. Catherines Ring (260 at 1800BC) and Sapelo Shell Ring (310 at 1500BC) [@sassaman2006]. Woodland civic and coastal centres peak at Crystal River (620 at 200AD), Letchworth Mounds (560 at 400AD), Kolomoki (1,65k at 600AD) and Bayshore Homes (520 at 700AD).

High Mississippian urbanism centres on Etowah (4,2k at 1300AD), Moundville (3,5k at 1300AD), Okmulgi (2,1k at 1100AD), Bottle Creek (1,4k at 1400AD), Irene Mound (1,15k at 1300AD), Pineland (920 at 1200AD), Rood's Landing (860 at 1300AD), Town Creek (820 at 1300AD), Safety Harbor (780 at 1350AD) and Singer-Moye (780 at 1300AD) [@king2003; @knight1998; @brown2003; @caldwell1941; @coe1995]. In the late pre-contact and early contact era from 1450AD to 1600AD, Mound Key (2,4k at 1550AD), Coosa (2,2k at 1550AD), Mabila (2,2k at 1540AD), Mulberry (1,8k at 1500AD), Lake Jackson Mounds (1,6k at 1500AD), Cofitachequi (1,45k at 1500AD), Anhaica (1,2k at 1539AD), Tukabatchee (1,2k at 1600AD), San Luis de Talimali (1,1k at 1600AD), Joara (920 at 1550AD) and Quiyoughcohannock (580 at 1600AD) anchor their regional provinces [@thompson2016; @hudson1997; @beck2016; @gallivan2016], alongside short-lived European colonies at Fort Caroline (300 in 1564AD) and Roanoke Island (117 in 1587AD) [@milanich1995; @quinn1985].

```{r tbl-included, results='asis'}
keys_inc <- names(sett_data)
peak_vals <- vapply(keys_inc, function (k) {
  vals <- as.numeric(unlist(sett_data[[k]]$population))
  if (length(vals) == 0) 0 else max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
}, numeric(1))
ord_top <- order(-peak_vals, keys_inc)
keys_top45 <- keys_inc[ord_top[seq_len(min(45L, length(ord_top)))]]
rows_inc <- lapply(keys_top45, function (k) {
  sv <- sett_data[[k]]
  data.frame(
    Region = clean_text(paste0(sv$name, " (", short_region(sv$region_id), ")")),
    Period = fmt_period_span(sv$population),
    Population = fmt_span_pop(sv$population),
    Bounds = paste0(viscount_fmt_number(sv$coords[[1]], 2L), ", ", viscount_fmt_number(sv$coords[[2]], 2L)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_inc <- do.call(rbind, rows_inc)
rownames(df_inc) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_inc,
  "Top 45 settlements by peak population in Southeast (HU 03) out of 115 catalogued sites, showing occupied spans and WGS84 coordinates.",
  c("Settlement (Division)", "Span", "Peak (Year)", "Coordinates"),
  list(label = "tab:se-included", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

## Excluded Ledger Candidates

One hundred and five candidate records in the regional source ledger (105 of 220) are excluded from the active point gazetteer: duplicate coordinate or variant-name aliases within 2 km of canonical sites merged into primary town series (such as Etowah, Mound Key, Okmulgi, Moundville, Mulberry, Bottle Creek, Coosa and Lake Jackson Mounds) to prevent double-counting [@king2003; @thompson2016].

```{r tbl-excluded, results='asis'}
exc_list <- Filter(function (c) identical(c$status, "excluded"), ledger_data$candidates)
exc_show <- head(exc_list, 30L)
rows_exc <- lapply(exc_show, function (c) {
  data.frame(
    Region = clean_text(paste0(c$name, " (", c$country, ")")),
    Period = "Excluded",
    Population = clean_text(c$reason),
    Bounds = clean_text(c$justification),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_exc <- do.call(rbind, rows_exc)
rownames(df_exc) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_exc,
  "Leading 30 of 105 excluded duplicate-alias candidate entries documented in the Southeast (HU 03) source ledger.",
  c("Candidate", "Status", "Reason", "Disposition"),
  list(label = "tab:se-excluded", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

# Limitations

Borderland settlements including Etowah, Coosa and Joara sit close to drainage margins shared with HU 06 (Cumberland and Tennessee) and are deduplicated during continental compilation so shared chiefdom seats are counted once. In addition, the remaining 70 smaller catalogued settlements below rank 45 (largely Palaeoindian springs, Archaic shell rings and secondary Woodland or Mississippian hamlets peaking between 35 and 540 inhabitants) are included in the underlying spatial subtraction grid even though Table \ref{tab:se-included} displays only the top 45 centres by peak population [@anderson1994; @milner2010].
